content.content:
I'm an associate professor of computer science at Purdue University. My research interests are in algorithmic game theory, theory of computation, artificial intelligence, algorithms, learning, computational complexity and their interface with dynamical systems and optimization. Example of topics I worked on include fair division, markets and auctions, games and learning dynamics, and the complexity of local search. My research is supported by an [NSF CAREER Award](https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2238372&HistoricalAwards=false).
See the [theory seminar](https://theorypurdue.wordpress.com/) (hybrid) and the [theory reading group](https://theory.cs.purdue.edu/spring2022.html).
I co-organized the [ACM EC 2024 Mentoring Workshop](https://sites.google.com/view/ec24mentoring/schedule-virtual), the [ACM EC 2023 Mentoring Workshop](https://sites.google.com/view/ec23mentoring/home?authuser=0), a [Mini-Symposium on Games and Learning](https://sites.google.com/view/games-canadam2023/home) at CanaDAM 2023, a [Workshop on Fair Division](https://www.fair-division-focs22.com/home) at FOCS 2022, and the [2019 Midwest Theory Day](https://sites.google.com/view/midwesttheoryday2019/home).
Current: [Reed C. Phillips](https://sites.google.com/view/reed-phillips/home) (Ph.D.)
Past: [Nicholas J. Recker](https://sites.google.com/view/nicholas-recker/home) ( [Ph.D.](https://hammer.purdue.edu/articles/thesis/Complexity_Bounds_for_Search_Problems/25620462)) [Nithish Kumar](https://www.cs.purdue.edu/people/graduate-students/kumar410.html) ( [Master's](https://hammer.purdue.edu/articles/thesis/Stochastic_Block_Model_Dynamics/14515080))
[The Query Complexity of Local Search in Rounds on General Graphs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.13266), Simina Brânzei, [Ioannis Panageas](https://panageas.github.io/), and [Dimitris Paparas](http://www.cs.columbia.edu/~paparas). Preprint.   **Note:** This paper is the result of an AI for math exploration. For the detailed case study, see the Google technical report below.
[Computing Envy-Free up to Any Good (EFX) Allocations via Local Search](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.05429), Simina Brânzei. Preprint. Code available [here](https://github.com/domnica/EFX).
[Searching, Sorting, and Cake Cutting in Rounds](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.00738), Simina Brânzei, [Dimitris Paparas](http://www.cs.columbia.edu/~paparas), and [Nicholas J. Recker](https://sites.google.com/view/nicholas-recker/home). Preprint.
[A note on quantum lower bounds for local search via congestion and expansion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.13345), Simina Brânzei and [Nicholas J. Recker](https://sites.google.com/view/nicholas-recker/home). Preprint.
[Accelerating Scientific Research with Gemini: Case Studies and Common Techniques,](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.03837) David Woodruff et al. Google technical report, 2026.
[Spectral Lower Bounds for Local Search](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.06248), Simina Brânzei and [Nicholas J. Recker](https://sites.google.com/view/nicholas-recker/home). In Electronic Journal of Combinatorics (to appear).
[Dueling over Multiple Pieces of Dessert](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.11486), Simina Brânzei and [Reed Phillips](https://sites.google.com/view/reed-phillips/home). In Proceedings of the 27th ACM Conference on Economics and Computation (ACM EC 2026).
[The Randomized Query Complexity of Finding a Tarski Fixed Point on the Boolean Hypercube](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.03751), Simina Brânzei, [Reed Phillips](https://www.cs.purdue.edu/people/graduate-students/phill289.html), and [Nicholas J. Recker](https://sites.google.com/view/nicholas-recker/home). In Discrete Mathematics, vol. 348, 2025. 
[Tarski Lower Bounds from Multi-Dimensional Herringbones](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.16679), Simina Brânzei, [Reed Phillips](https://www.cs.purdue.edu/people/graduate-students/phill289.html), and [Nicholas J. Recker](https://sites.google.com/view/nicholas-recker/home). In Proceedings of the International Conference on Randomization and Computation (RANDOM 2025). 
[Tit-for-Tat Strategies Drive Growth and Inequality in Production Economies](https://royalsocietypublishing.org/doi/epdf/10.1098/rspa.2024.0533), Simina Brânzei, [Ruta Mehta](http://rutamehta.cs.illinois.edu/), and [Noam Nisan](http://www.cs.huji.ac.il/~noam/). In [Proceedings of the Royal Society A: Mathematical, Physical, and Engineering Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proceedings_of_the_Royal_Society), vol. 481, 2025. 
(Abstract in [NeurIPS 2018](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2018/file/692f93be8c7a41525c0baf2076aecfb4-Paper.pdf)). 
[Dueling over Dessert, Mastering the Art of Repeated Cake Cutting](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.08547.pdf), Simina Brânzei, [MohammadTaghi Hajiaghayi](https://www.cs.umd.edu/~hajiagha/), [Reed Phillips](https://www.cs.purdue.edu/people/graduate-students/phill289.html), [Suho Shin](https://suhoshin.github.io/), and [Kun Wang](https://a865143034.github.io/). In Proceedings of the 38th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2024). Here are the [slides](https://simina.info/WALE_2024_repeated_cake_cutting.pdf) from [WALE 2024](https://wale.gr/2024/) talk.
[The Sharp Power Law of Local Search on Expanders](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.08269), Simina Brânzei, [Davin Choo](http://davinchoo.com/), and [Nicholas J. Recker](https://sites.google.com/view/nicholas-recker/home). In Proceedings of the ACM-SIAM Symposium on Discrete Algorithms (SODA 2024).
[Tit-for-Tat Dynamics and Market Volatility](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.03629), Simina Brânzei. In [Nonlinearity](https://iopscience.iop.org/journal/0951-7715), vol. 37, issue 3, pp. 035006, IOP Publishing & London Mathematical Society, 2024.
[Algorithms for Competitive Division of Chores](https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/abs/10.1287/moor.2023.1361?journalCode=moor), Simina Brânzei and [Fedor Sandomirskiy](https://fedors.info/). In Mathematics of Operations Research, vol. 49, issue 1, pp. 398-429, 2024.
[Learning and Collusion in Multi-unit Auctions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.17402), Simina Brânzei, [Mahsa Derakhshan](https://www.khoury.northeastern.edu/home/derakhshan/), [Negin Golrezaei](https://www.mit.edu/~golrezae/), and [Yanjun Han](https://yanjunhan2021.github.io/). In Proceedings of the 37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2023).
[Phase Transitions of Diversity in Stochastic Block Model Dynamics](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.13713), Simina Brânzei, [Nithish Kumar](https://www.cs.purdue.edu/people/graduate-students/kumar410.html), and [Gireeja Ranade](http://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~gireeja/). In Proceedings of the 59th Allerton Conference on Communication, Control, and Computing ( [Allerton 2023](https://allerton.csl.illinois.edu/)).
[Walrasian Pricing in Multi-unit Auctions](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0004370223001078?via%3Dihub), Simina Brânzei, [Aris Filos-Ratsikas](http://arisfilosratsikas.com/), [Peter Bro Miltersen](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=0za9d6AAAAAJ&hl=en&oi=ao), and Yulong Zeng. In Artificial Intelligence, 2023.
Preliminary version in Proceedings of the International Symposium on Mathematical Foundations of Computer Science ( [MFCS 2017](http://mfcs2017.cs.aau.dk/index.shtml)).
[Nash Social Welfare Approximation for Strategic Agents](https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/10.1287/opre.2020.2056), Simina Brânzei, [Vasilis Gkatzelis](https://www.cs.drexel.edu/~gkatz/), and [Ruta Mehta](http://rutamehta.cs.illinois.edu/). In [Operations Research](https://pubsonline.informs.org/journal/opre), 2022.
Preliminary version in Proceedings of the 18th ACM conference on Economics and Computation ( [ACM EC 2017](http://www.sigecom.org/ec17/)). Here is a [video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Vfb_6Q-zMhw&list=PLI0o-KVQWwQ-j0BPLDP6Rytpn35X23Xpg&index=64) of the talk.
[The Query Complexity of Local Search and Brouwer in Rounds](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.00061), Simina Brânzei and [Jiawei Li](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~davidlee/). In Proceedings of the 35th Annual Conference on Learning Theory ( [COLT 2022](http://learningtheory.org/colt2022/)). Minor revision in [Mathematical Statistics and Learning](https://ems.press/journals/msl). 
[The Query Complexity of Cake Cutting](file:///usr/local/google/home/sbranzei/Downloads/Simina_files/Cake_query_polished.pdf), Simina Brânzei and [Noam Nisan](http://www.cs.huji.ac.il/~noam/). In Proceedings of the 36th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems ( [NeurIPS 2022](https://nips.cc/)).
[How to Charge Lightning: The Economics of Bitcoin Transaction Channels](https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.10222), Simina Brânzei, [Erel Segal-Halevi](http://tora.us.fm/erelsgl/), and [Aviv Zohar](http://www.avivz.net/). In Proceedings of the 58th Allerton Conference on Communication, Control, and Computing ( [Allerton 2022](https://allerton.csl.illinois.edu/)).
[Exchange Markets: Proportional Response Dynamics and Beyond](https://www.sigecom.org/exchanges/volume_19/2/BRANZEI.pdf), Simina Brânzei. In [ACM SIGecom Exchanges 2021](https://www.sigecom.org/exchanges/).
[P4-free Partition and Cover Numbers](https://eprint.iacr.org/2020/1605), [Alexander Block](https://www.cs.purdue.edu/homes/block9/), Simina Brânzei, [Hemanta K. ## Biography

Anuran Makur is an Assistant Professor with the Department of Computer Science ( [CS](https://www.cs.purdue.edu/ "Purdue CS Homepage")) and the Elmore Family School of Electrical and Computer Engineering ( [ECE](https://engineering.purdue.edu/ECE "Purdue ECE Homepage")), [Purdue University](https://www.purdue.edu/ "Purdue Homepage"), West Lafayette, IN, USA. He received the B.S. degree with highest honors ( _summa cum laude_) from the Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences ( [EECS](https://eecs.berkeley.edu/ "UC Berkeley EECS Department Homepage")), University of California, Berkeley ( [UC Berkeley](http://www.berkeley.edu/ "UC Berkeley Homepage")), CA, USA, in 2013, and the S.M. and Sc.D. degrees from the Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science ( [EECS](https://www.eecs.mit.edu/ "MIT EECS Department Homepage")), Massachusetts Institute of Technology ( [MIT](http://www.mit.edu/ "MIT Homepage")), Cambridge, MA, USA, in 2015 and 2019, respectively. From 2019 to 2021, he was a postdoctoral researcher at the Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems ( [LIDS](https://lids.mit.edu/ "MIT LIDS Homepage")) and the Institute for Data, Systems, and Society ( [IDSS](https://idss.mit.edu/ "MIT IDSS Homepage")), MIT. His research interests include information theory, theory of machine learning, and applied probability. He was a recipient of the [Arthur M. Hopkin Award](https://www2.eecs.berkeley.edu/Students/Awards/9/ "UC Berkeley EECS Arthur M. Hopkin Award") from UC Berkeley in 2013, the Jacobs [Presidential Fellowship](https://web.mit.edu/provost/presfellow/ "MIT Presidential Fellowship") from MIT in 2013, the Ernst A. Guillemin Master's Thesis Award from MIT in 2015, the Jin Au Kong Doctoral Thesis Award from MIT in 2020, the [Thomas M. Cover Dissertation Award](https://www.itsoc.org/honors/cover-award "IEEE Information Theory Society Thomas M. Cover Dissertation Award") from the IEEE Information Theory Society in 2021, and the [CAREER Award](https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2337808 "NSF CAREER Award") from the National Science Foundation in 2023.

See his Purdue CS profile [here](https://www.cs.purdue.edu/people/faculty/amakur.html) and ECE profile [here](https://engineering.purdue.edu/ECE/People/ptProfile?resource_id=258037).

## Mentees

I am passionate about mentoring the next generation of researchers. Below are the talented individuals I have had the privilege to mentor and collaborate with:

[https://ecoai-group.github.io/team/](https://ecoai-group.github.io/team/)

* * *

### For Prospective Mentees

I am always looking to work with motivated students interested in computer architecture, computer systems, and AI. If you are interested in working with me, please review my recent publications, then reach out via email with your CV, transcript, and a summary of your past research experience attached. I apologize ahead of time if I don’t have the bandwidth to reply to every inquiry email, but we’ll make sure to review everyone’s profile.

# Team Members
![](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/ce7e81_39e12457d4f843b6a8b83ffbc8f97e4b~mv2.jpeg/v1/fill/w_279,h_285,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/Image-empty-state.jpeg)
## Weiruo Zhang
Assistant Professor
Weiruo earned her Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering from Stanford University. For her doctoral study, she worked with Dr. David Dill in Computer Science of Stanford University, developing graph based machine learning (ML) algorithms for metabolomics data. Weiruo later worked with Dr. Sylvia Plevritis in Stanford School of medicine, with research focus of implementing ML/AI approaches to integrate multi-modality data to study tumor progression. Outside the lab, she enjoys piano, reading, oil painting, and watching soccer.
![](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/ce7e81_6943b2d95e3042409b852d9c5643adc9~mv2.jpeg/v1/fill/w_279,h_285,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/Image-empty-state.jpeg)
## Harshini Magesh
Undergraduate student
Harshini is a senior majoring in Computer Science with a concentration in Machine Intelligence and a minor in Mathematics at Purdue University. Her research interests center on leveraging machine learning and computational modeling to advance data-driven discovery in biology and medicine. Outside of research, Harshini enjoys singing, music production and exploring the creative applications of technology.
![](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/ce7e81_3705c42a6dbe4bdeb56335f6dc33eb71~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_279,h_285,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/Image-empty-state.jpg)
## Yunyi Gao
Graduate student
Yunyi is currently a Computer Science (CS) graduate student at Tufts University. Yunyi completed her Undergraduate studies in CS at Purdue, during which she worked in our lab as a research assistant. Yunyi continues working with us currently on a spatial multi-omics integration project.
![](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/ce7e81_d369d4bc9f6c4d4b8d893d0c20eb803b~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_279,h_285,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/Image-empty-state.png)
## Kyenret Yakubu Ayuba
PhD student
Kyenret is a PhD student in the PULSe program. She earned her B.S. in Biomedical Engineering from Purdue University. Her research includes developing machine learning and molecular simulation pipelines for protein interactions and drug discovery, as well as computational and statistical approaches to investigate gene-environment interactions in admixed populations. In her free time, she enjoys reading and watching movies and documentaries.
![](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/ce7e81_1efae4de490148839552f4b18917605e~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_279,h_285,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/Image-empty-state.jpg)
## Harsha Srirangam
Undergraduate student
Harsha is a second-year undergraduate student studying Applied Mathematics and Computer Science. His previous work spans natural language processing, computer vision, computational biology, and cancer metabolomics, and he is more broadly interested in developing biological foundation models with multi-omic data. In his free time, he enjoys playing basketball, watching and reading sci-fi, and making origami.
![](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/ce7e81_c7f358c9b8f944e18da00abb710cab27~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_279,h_285,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/Image-empty-state.jpg)
## Md. Ishrak Ahsan
PhD student
Ishrak is a PhD student in Computer Science. He received his B.Sc. in Computer Science and Engineering from the Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET). He is interested in developing computational and machine learning methods for analyzing single-cell and spatial transcriptomics data and exploring their applications in health and disease. Beyond research, he enjoys watching movies, TV series, and exploring new places.
![](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/ce7e81_ce58c650be8e47659b7e1b6699f08609~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_279,h_285,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/Image-empty-state.png)
## Rashmi Bhaskara
PhD student
Rashimi is a PhD student in Medical Physics, co-supervised by Dr. Oluwaseyi Oderinde and Dr. Zhang. Rashimi completed her MS from Computer Science at Purdue. Her work is broadly focused on using AI and medical imaging to better understand the tumor microenvironment and cancer treatment response.

## About Me [Link to heading 'About Me'](https://gitlab.com/mshahbaz/mshahbaz.gitlab.io/-/wikis/home\#about-me)

I am an **Assistant Professor** of [Computer Science and Engineering](https://cse.engin.umich.edu/) at the [University of Michigan](https://umich.edu/), where I direct the [NextGArch Lab](https://nextgarch.github.io/).

I am broadly interested in computer systems, networks, and architecture. At Michigan, I work on designing and building domain-specific (performance) abstractions, compilers, and architectures for next-generation networks and systems and their applications to emerging workloads (including machine learning, self-driving networks, serverless/edge compute, and 5G).

Before joining Michigan, I was a Kevin C. and Suzanne L. Kahn New Frontiers Assistant Professor in Computer Science at [Purdue University](https://www.cs.purdue.edu/). I did my postdoc at [Stanford University](https://www.stanford.edu/) and got my Ph.D. and M.A. in Computer Science from [Princeton University](https://www.princeton.edu/) as well as a B.E. in Computer Engineering from [National University of Sciences and Technology (NUST)](http://nust.edu.pk/).

I am married to [Saira Malik](https://saira.shahbaz.org/).

> **Prospective Students and Postdocs:** The world of computing systems is _changing_; [email me](mailto:msbaz@umich.edu) and [apply here](https://cse.engin.umich.edu/academics/graduate/admissions/) if you are interested in driving this _change_ with me at the University of Michigan! You can learn more about my advising and mentorship style [here](https://cse.engin.umich.edu/people/faculty/mentor/msbaz).

## Computational Vegetation Lab at Purdue University

_Computational Vegetation Lab_ focuses on digital twins of plants, particularly on digital tree models. We research the shape, structure, and function of vegetation. We study the plant’s shape, development over time, and interaction with its environment (light, water, wind, temperature). Most of the work has been done in collaboration with our colleagues and past members, listed on the [Members](https://www.cs.purdue.edu/compveg/members/) page.

![](https://www.cs.purdue.edu/compveg/images/vegetation/veg-group.jpg)

##### Welcome to the **Co** mputational **M** otion, **M** anipulation, and **A** utonomy (CoMMA) lab at [Purdue](https://www.purdue.edu/)!

## About Us

**We make robots move!**

Our research broadly covers algorithms, methods, and software that enable complex robots (or other autonomous systems) to achieve complicated tasks. Usually our research views problems through the lens of _planning_: we build or learn models of the robot and its environment, and use those models to reason over how actions move the robot, and thus how to achieve a goal. We are interested in techniques that generalize to any robot, constraint, task, or environment, and that are fast, efficient, and easy to use—we want our approaches to apply to robots that work in factories, homes, hospitals, and even space! We are also interested in the intersection of the theory and practice of robotics algorithms, finding where software engineering, hardware acceleration, and algorithm design work together to build systems fast enough to run in real time.

27:Social support plays a crucial role in managing and enhancing one’s mental health and well-being. In order to explore the role of a robot’s companion-like behavior on its therapeutic interventions, we conducted an eight-week-long deployment study with seventy participants to compare the impact of (1) a control robot with only assistant-like skills, (2) a coach-like robot with additional instructive positive psychology interventions, and (3) a companion-like robot that delivered the same interventions in a peer-like and supportive manner. The companion-like robot was shown to be the most effective in building a positive therapeutic alliance with people, enhancing participants’ well-being and readiness for change. Our work offers valuable insights into how companion AI agents could further enhance the efficacy of the mental health interventions by strengthening their therapeutic alliance with people for long-term mental health support.
35:Positive Psychology for College Students
37:Many college students suffer from mental health issues that impact their physical, social, and occupational outcomes. Various scalable technologies have been proposed in order to mitigate the negative impact of mental health disorders. We explore the use of a social robot coach to deliver positive psychology interventions to college students living in on-campus dormitories. A one-week deployment study with 35 college students showed that our robotic intervention improved participants' psychological wellbeing, mood, and readiness to change behavior. We also found that students' personality traits had a significant association with intervention efficacy.
41:\*Best Paper Award\* and \*Best Student Paper Finalist\* at RO-MAN 2020
67:Children and their parents undergo challenging experiences when admitted for inpatient care at pediatric hospitals. We aim to close this gap by creating a social robot that can mitigate pediatric patients' stress/anxiety/pain by engaging them in playful interactive activities. We conducted a randomized control trial that compare the effects of the Huggable robot to a virtual character on a screen and a plush teddy bear at Boston Children's Hospital with 54 pediatric inpatients in MSICU, Oncology and Surgical units. The study showed that social robot's physical embodiment has significant impact on children and their caregivers' engagement and socio-emotional interactions. This work was done in collaboration with Boston Children's Hospital and Northeastern University.

87:Prior research has established that dialogic reading, the process of having a dialogue with students around the text they are reading, is an effective method for expanding young children’s vocabulary. In this project, we asked whether a social robot can effectively engage preschoolers in dialogic reading, and whether the robot's verbal expressiveness impacted children’s learning and engagement during a dialogic reading activity. Our study showed that children learned from the robot, emulated the robot’s story during the story retelling, and treated the robot as a social being. However, children showed more engagement and were more likely to identify target vocabulary words after interacting with a robot with expressive voice than with a robot with flat voice. Taken together, these results suggest that children may benefit more from the expressive robot than from the flat robot.

I am a Masters student in the CoMMA lab in the [Computer Science Department](https://www.cs.purdue.edu/) of [Purdue University](https://www.purdue.edu/). I am currently working on learning-based motion planning and trajectory optimization for realtime (millisecond!) planning.

I’m still sorting out my research interests, which broadly involve designing robotic systems and algorithms that can make informed adaptations to unseen and ever-changing conditions in the real world. Sometimes, this involves distilling high level semantic information into executable trajectories and motions.

In the past, I have worked on projects spanning kinodynamic motion planning for wacky situations, distributed multiagent RL, open language querying, and human-robot interaction/intent modelling. I am also interested in how we can make proof-of-concept methods from literature reliable and explainable enough to deploy to commercial robots.

content.content:
# IDEAS Lab

Welcome to the interdisciplinary research lab, IDEAS (Intelligent Design for Exploration and Augmented
Systems), housed within Purdue Computer Science. Our lab is dedicated to advancing state-of-the-art in
robotics, computer vision, AI, and virtual environments. Our research bridges multiple domains, with a strong
emphasis on leveraging human-centered insights and machine intelligence to tackle real-world challenges in
robotics, computer vision/graphics, and artificial intelligence.

[Explore Research →](https://ideas.cs.purdue.edu/research/) [Meet the Team](https://ideas.cs.purdue.edu/people/)

Research Themes

Motion Planning, Neural Models for Planning and Prediction, Computer Vision and Graphics,
Human-Agent Interaction and Simulation, Field and Aerial Robotics, Generative AI.

# People
Welcome to the interdisciplinary research lab, IDEAS (Intelligent Design for Exploration and Augmented Systems), housed within Purdue Computer Science. Our lab is dedicated to advancing state-of-the-art in robotics, computer vision, AI, and virtual environments. Our research bridges multiple domains, with a strong emphasis on leveraging human-centered insights and machine intelligence to tackle real-world challenges in robotics, computer vision/graphics, and artificial intelligence.
If you are an undergraduate or graduate student interested in joining our lab, please contact us at [aniketbera@purdue.edu](mailto:aniketbera@purdue.edu).

1. [IROS](https://ieee-iros.org/) Vectorizing Projection in Manifold-Constrained Motion Planning for Real-Time Whole-Body Control [Shrutheesh R. Iyer](https://commalab.org/members/shrutheesh), [I-Chia Chang](https://www.linkedin.com/in/i-chia-chang-880063256/), Andrew Z. Liu, [Yan Gu](https://www.thetracelab.com/ygu.html/), and [Zachary Kingston](https://commalab.org/members/kingston) _In IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems_ To Appear AbsBib [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.13323) [Code](https://github.com/CoMMALab/vamp/tree/constrained_planner?tab=readme-ov-file#manifold-constrained-planner) [Website](https://commalab.org/papers/mcvamp) Many robot planning tasks require satisfaction of one or more constraints throughout the entire trajectory. For geometric constraints, manifold-constrained motion planning algorithms are capable of planning collision-free path between start and goal configurations on the constraint submanifolds specified by task. Current state-of-the-art methods can take tens of seconds to solve these tasks for complex systems such as humanoid robots, making real-world use impractical, especially in dynamic settings. Inspired by recent advances in hardware accelerated motion planning, we present a CPU SIMD-accelerated manifold-constrained motion planner that revisits projection-based constraint satisfaction through the lens of parallelization. By transforming relevant components into parallelizable structures, we use SIMD parallelism to plan constraint satisfying solutions. Our approach achieves up to 100-1000x speed-ups over the state-of-the-art, making real-time constrained motion planning feasible for the first time. We demonstrate our planner on a real humanoid robot and show real-time whole-body quasi-static plan generation. @inproceedings{iyer2026mcvamp,
  author = {Iyer, Shrutheesh R. and Chang, I-Chia and Liu, Andrew Z. and Gu, Yan and Kingston, Zachary},
  booktitle = {IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems},
  note = {To Appear},
  title = {Vectorizing Projection in Manifold-Constrained Motion Planning for Real-Time Whole-Body Control},
  year = {2026}
}
2. [IROS](https://ieee-iros.org/)![hjcdik.jpg](https://commalab.org/assets/img/publication_preview/hjcdik.jpg) HJCD-IK: GPU-Accelerated Inverse Kinematics through Batched Hybrid Jacobian Coordinate Descent [Cael Yasutake](https://caelyasutake.github.io/), [Andrew H. Liu](https://commalab.org/members/andy), [Zachary Kingston](https://commalab.org/members/kingston), and [Brian Plancher](https://brianplancher.com/) _In IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems_ To Appear AbsBib [PDF](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.07514) [Code](https://github.com/a2r-lab/HJCD-IK) [Website](https://a2r-lab.org/HJCD-IK/) Inverse Kinematics (IK) is a core problem in robotics, in which joint configurations are found to achieve a desired end-effector pose. Although analytical solvers are fast and efficient, they are limited to systems with low degrees-of-freedom and specific topological structures. Numerical optimization-based approaches are more general, but suffer from high computational costs and frequent convergence to spurious local minima. Recent efforts have explored the use of GPUs to combine sampling and optimization to enhance both the accuracy and speed of IK solvers. We build on this recent literature and introduce HJCD-IK, a GPU-accelerated, sampling-based hybrid solver that combines an orientation-aware greedy coordinate descent initialization scheme with a Jacobian-based polishing routine. This design enables our solver to improve both convergence speed and overall accuracy as compared to the state-of-the-art, consistently finding solutions along the accuracy-latency Pareto frontier and often achieving order-of-magnitude gains. In addition, our method produces a broad distribution of high-quality samples, yielding the lowest maximum mean discrepancy. We release our code open-source for the benefit of the community. @inproceedings{yasutake2026hjcdik,
  author = {Yasutake, Cael and Liu, Andrew H. and Kingston, Zachary and Plancher, Brian},
  booktitle = {IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems},
  note = {To Appear},
  title = {{HJCD-IK}: {GPU}-Accelerated Inverse Kinematics through Batched Hybrid Jacobian Coordinate Descent},
  year = {2026}
}
3. [IROS](https://ieee-iros.org/) NeHMO: Neural Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability Learning for Decentralized Safe Multi-Agent Motion Planning [Qingyi Chen](https://commalab.org/members/qingyi_chen), [Zachary Kingston](https://commalab.org/members/kingston), and [Ahmed H. Qureshi](https://qureshiahmed.github.io/) _In IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems_ To Appear AbsBib [PDF](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00326) [Video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IZiePX0p1Mc) [Code](https://github.com/qingyichen/nehmo-dev) Safe multi-arm motion planning is a challenging problem in robotics due to its high dimensionality, coupled configuration space, and complex collision constraints. Centralized planners are capable of coordinating all arms but often face scalability limitations, restricting applicability in real-time settings. On the other hand, decentralized methods are scalable and recent deep learning-based approaches have shown promising results. However, these depend on accurate behavior prediction or coordination protocols and may fail when other arms act unpredictably. To address these challenges, we introduce a neural Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability (HJR) learning-based approach to approximate a safety value function that captures worst-case inter-arm safety constraints. We further develop a decentralized trajectory optimization framework that uses the learned HJR representation for real-time planning. The proposed method is scalable and data-efficient, generalizes across multi-manipulator systems, and outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on challenging multi-arm motion planning tasks. @inproceedings{chen2026nehmo,
  author = {Chen, Qingyi and Kingston, Zachary and Qureshi, Ahmed H.},
  booktitle = {IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems},
  note = {To Appear},
  title = {{NeHMO}: Neural {Hamilton-Jacobi} Reachability Learning for Decentralized Safe Multi-Agent Motion Planning},
  year = {2026}
}
4. [IROS](https://ieee-iros.org/) Fast Asymptotically Optimal Kinodynamic Planning via Vectorization [Yitian Gao](https://commalab.org/members/yitian), [Andrew Lu](https://commalab.org/members/andrew-lu), and [Zachary Kingston](https://commalab.org/members/kingston) _In IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems_ To Appear AbsBib [PDF](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.03987) [Video](https://youtu.be/EjxSVqkC3sk) [Code](https://github.com/CoMMALab/pakr) [Website](https://commalab.org/papers/pakr) Sampling-based motion planners have been shown to be effective for systems with complex kinodynamic constraints and high dimensionality. However, these algorithms struggle to achieve real-time performance, leading to recent efforts to parallelize planning. While GPU-accelerated planners have achieved significant speedups, existing approaches require specialized CUDA programming that limits accessibility and portability. We present Parallel Asymptotically Optimal Kinodynamic RRT (PAKR), a massively parallel kinodynamic planner leveraging JAX and the XLA compiler to achieve GPU acceleration through standard Python tooling. By combining our parallel planner with the AO-x meta-algorithm, we achieve asymptotic optimality through fast iterative replanning. We provide a theoretical analysis of probabilistic completeness, analyze the effects of batch size and branching factor on convergence, and demonstrate scalability to complex dynamics using the MuJoCo-XLA simulator. Experiments show competitive runtimes with state-of-the-art GPU planners and superior solution quality. @inproceedings{gao2026pakr,
  author = {Gao, Yitian and Lu, Andrew and Kingston, Zachary},
  booktitle = {IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems},
  note = {To Appear},
  title = {Fast Asymptotically Optimal Kinodynamic Planning via Vectorization},
  year = {2026}
}
5. [IROS](https://ieee-iros.org/)![cde.png](https://commalab.org/assets/img/publication_preview/cde.png) CDE: Concept-Driven Exploration for Reinforcement Learning Le Mao, [Andrew H. Liu](https://commalab.org/members/andy), Renos Zabounidis, Yanan Niu, [Zachary Kingston](https://commalab.org/members/kingston), and [Joseph Campbell](https://joe-campbell.github.io/website/) _In IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems_ To Appear AbsBib [PDF](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.08851) [Code](https://github.com/LeMaoLeMao/Concept-Learning) [Website](https://sites.google.com/view/concept-learn/home) Intelligent exploration remains a critical challenge in reinforcement learning (RL), especially in visual control tasks. Unlike low-dimensional state-based RL, visual RL must extract task-relevant structure from raw pixels, making exploration inefficient. We propose Concept-Driven Exploration (CDE), which leverages a pre-trained vision-language model (VLM) to generate object-centric visual concepts from textual task descriptions as weak, potentially noisy supervisory signals. Rather than directly conditioning on these noisy signals, CDE trains a policy to reconstruct the concepts via an auxiliary objective, using reconstruction accuracy as an intrinsic reward to guide exploration toward task-relevant objects. Because the policy internalizes these concepts, VLM queries are only needed during training, reducing dependence on external models during deployment. Across five challenging simulated visual manipulation tasks, CDE achieves efficient, targeted exploration and remains robust to noisy VLM predictions. Finally, we demonstrate real-world transfer by deploying CDE on a Franka Research 3 arm, attaining an 80% success rate in a real-world manipulation task. @inproceedings{mao2026cde,
  author = {Mao, Le and Liu, Andrew H. and Zabounidis, Renos and Niu, Yanan and Kingston, Zachary and Campbell, Joseph},
  booktitle = {IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems},
  note = {To Appear},
  title = {{CDE}: Concept-Driven Exploration for Reinforcement Learning},
  year = {2026}
}
6. [ICRA](https://ieee-icra.org/) pRRTC: GPU-Parallel RRT-Connect for Fast, Consistent, and Low-Cost Motion Planning Chih H. Huang*, [Pranav Jadhav*](https://commalab.org/members/jadhav), [Brian Plancher](https://brianplancher.com/), and [Zachary Kingston](https://commalab.org/members/kingston) _In IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation_ AbsBib [PDF](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.06757) [Video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=okpqftLB6P8) [Code](https://github.com/CoMMALab/pRRTC) [Website](https://commalab.org/papers/pRRTC) Sampling-based motion planning algorithms, like the Rapidly-Exploring Random Tree (RRT) and its widely used variant, RRT-Connect, provide efficient solutions for high-dimensional planning problems faced by real-world robots. However, these methods remain computationally intensive, particularly in complex environments that require many collision checks. As such, to improve performance, recent efforts have explored parallelizing specific components of RRT, such as collision checking or running multiple planners independently, but no prior work has integrated parallelism at multiple levels of the algorithm for robotic manipulation. In this work, we present pRRTC, a GPU-accelerated implementation of RRT-Connect that achieves parallelism across the entire algorithm through multithreaded expansion and connection, SIMT-optimized collision checking, and hierarchical parallelism optimization, improving efficiency, consistency, and initial solution cost. We evaluate the effectiveness of pRRTC on the MotionBenchMaker dataset using robots with 7, 8, and 14 degrees-of-freedom, demonstrating up to 6x average speedup on constrained reaching tasks at high collision checking resolution compared to state-of-the-art. pRRTC also demonstrates a 5x reduction in solution time variance and 1.5x improvement in initial path costs compared to state-of-the-art motion planners in complex environments across all robots. @inproceedings{huangjadhav2026prrtc,
  author = {Huang, Chih H. and Jadhav, Pranav and Plancher, Brian and Kingston, Zachary},
  booktitle = {IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation},
  doi = {10.1109/ICRA57385.2026.11696901},
  pages = {5892--5899},
  title = {{pRRTC}: {GPU}-Parallel {RRT}-Connect for Fast, Consistent, and Low-Cost Motion Planning},
  year = {2026}
}
7. [ICRA](https://ieee-icra.org/) Parallel Heuristic Search as Inference for Actor-Critic Reinforcement Learning Models [Hanlan Yang](https://commalab.org/members/hanlan), [Itamar Mishani](https://imishani.github.io/), Luca Pivetti, [Zachary Kingston](https://commalab.org/members/kingston), and [Maxim Likhachev](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~maxim/) _In IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation_ AbsBib [PDF](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.25402) Actor-Critic models are a class of model-free deep reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms that have demonstrated effectiveness across various robot learning tasks. While considerable research has focused on improving training stability and data sampling efficiency, most deployment strategies have remained relatively simplistic, typically relying on direct actor policy rollouts. In contrast, we propose PACHS (Parallel Actor-Critic Heuristic Search), an efficient parallel best-first search algorithm for inference that leverages both components of the actor-critic architecture: the actor network generates actions, while the critic network provides cost-to-go estimates to guide the search. Two levels of parallelism are employed within the search – actions and cost-to-go estimates are generated in batches by the actor and critic networks respectively, and graph expansion is distributed across multiple threads. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in robotic manipulation tasks, including collision-free motion planning and contact-rich interactions such as non-prehensile pushing. @inproceedings{yang2026pachs,
  author = {Yang, Hanlan and Mishani, Itamar and Pivetti, Luca and Kingston, Zachary and Likhachev, Maxim},
  booktitle = {IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation},
  doi = {10.1109/ICRA57385.2026.11697579},
  pages = {14441--14448},
  title = {Parallel Heuristic Search as Inference for Actor-Critic Reinforcement Learning Models},
  year = {2026}
}
8. [ICRA](https://ieee-icra.org/) Differentiable Particle Optimization for Fast Sequential Manipulation [Lucas Chen](https://commalab.org/members/lucas), [Shrutheesh R. Iyer](https://commalab.org/members/shrutheesh), and [Zachary Kingston](https://commalab.org/members/kingston) _In IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation_ AbsBib [PDF](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.07674) [Video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VK8PYsdXNBk) [Code](https://github.com/CoMMALab/SPaSM) [Website](https://commalab.org/papers/spasm) Sequential robot manipulation tasks require finding collision-free trajectories that satisfy geometric constraints across multiple object interactions in potentially high-dimensional configuration spaces. Solving these problems in real-time and at large scales has remained out of reach due to computational requirements. Recently, GPU-based acceleration has shown promising results, but prior methods achieve limited performance due to CPU-GPU data transfer overhead and complex logic that prevents full hardware utilization. To this end, we present SPaSM (Sampling Particle optimization for Sequential Manipulation), a fully GPU-parallelized framework that compiles constraint evaluation, sampling, and gradient-based optimization into optimized CUDA kernels for end-to-end trajectory optimization without CPU coordination. The method consists of a two-stage particle optimization strategy: first solving placement constraints through massively parallel sampling, then lifting solutions to full trajectory optimization in joint space. Unlike hierarchical approaches, SPaSM jointly optimizes object placements and robot trajectories to handle scenarios where motion feasibility constrains placement options. Experimental evaluation on challenging benchmarks demonstrates solution times in the realm of milliseconds with a 100% success rate; a 4000x speedup compared to existing approaches. @inproceedings{chen2026spasm,

30:- \[Aug. 2025\] [SecureChain](https://github.com/purdue-hcss/SecureChain) has been selected for NSF’s National AI Research Resource (NAIRR) Pilot! [NSF news](https://www.nsf.gov/news/nsf-expanding-national-ai-infrastructure-new-data-systems), [Purdue news](https://www.cs.purdue.edu/news/article
# HCSS Lab
Welcome to Human-Centered Software Systems Lab
The **Human-Centered Software Systems Lab**, led by [_Dr. Tianyi Zhang_](https://tianyi-zhang.github.io/) at [Purdue University](https://www.purdue.edu/), focuses on the development of intelligent systems that integrate human expertise with machine intelligence. The lab's research lies at the intersection of _Software Engineering_, _Human-Computer Interaction_, and _AI_, with a primary goal of enhancing programming productivity and software robustness. Their work encompasses various areas, including:
- **Code Mining and Visualization**: Unveiling what others have and have not done in similar programming contexts in platforms like [GitHub](https://github.com/) and [Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/) to help programmers make more informed decisions. Their work in this area has been presented at [ICSE 2018](https://conf.researchr.org/home/icse-2018), [CHI 2018](https://chi2018.acm.org/), [ICSE 2019](https://conf.researchr.org/home/icse-2019), [CHI 2020](https://chi2020.acm.org/), [CHI 2021a](https://chi2021.acm.org/), and [UIST 2022a](https://uist.acm.org/uist2022/).
- **Program Synthesis**: Enabling novices and end-users to better communicate their intent and guide synthesizers through enriched feedback loops and interpretability. Their contributions in this field have been showcased in [UIST 2020](https://uist.acm.org/uist2020/), [CHI 2021b](https://chi2021.acm.org/), and [UIST 2022b](https://uist.acm.org/uist2022/).
- **Autonomous Driving Testing**: Enhancing the understanding of developer needs in testing autonomous driving systems, and enabling the expression of richer and more efficient test scenarios. Their research on autonomous driving testing has been presented at [ESEC/FSE 2022a](https://2022.esec-fse.org/), [ESEC/FSE 2022b](https://2022.esec-fse.org/), and [TSE 2022](https://www.computer.org/conferences/transactions-on-software-engineering/).
The lab also conducts research in other areas such as _code search_, _test reuse_, _software debloating_, and _empirical studies on deep learning engineering_. Notably, they have collaborated with psychiatrists at Harvard Medical School and Massachusetts General Hospital to explore massive amounts of health records and develop data-driven insights about disease progression and treatment trajectories, as presented in [VAHC 2021](https://precisionmedicine.hm.harvard.edu/vahc/).
Through their interdisciplinary approach, the Human-Centered Software Systems Lab strives to create interactive intelligent systems that augment human intelligence with data-driven insights and augment machine intelligence with human guidance. Their research benefits a wide range of individuals in the programming domain, including software developers, novice programmers, and computer end-users.

content.text:
I wrote all 9 entries to `/tmp/fceval-a4-t1-ycda4mmj/work/results/b4.json`. Two people have no student list, and Kingston's count is uncertain because his lab's team page wouldn't load.

- **Tamal K. Dey**: 5 PhD students, from the "Current" personnel table on his homepage. His CGTDA lab site's people page is outdated: the 5 students it lists are under "Past" on his homepage. 2025 paper: "Decomposing multiparameter persistence modules", SoCG 2025 (homepage).
- **Tianyi Zhang**: students not listed anywhere. I found his lab site (hcss.cs.purdue.edu) by web search; it has no people page and its news stops in June 2023. 2025 paper: "Active Layer-Contrastive Decoding Reduces Hallucination in Large Language Model Generation", EMNLP 2025 (homepage).
- **Vamsi Addanki**: 6 PhD students on the STyGIANet people page; Eliezer and Mahir are co-advised. One conflict: an August 2025 news item calls Deeksha P. Rao a Masters student, but the people page now lists her as a PhD student. 2025 paper: "Pyrrha: …", NSDI 2025 (homepage). He joined Purdue in fall 2025.
- **Yexiang Xue**: students not listed; his homepage only names undergraduates he mentored at Cornell, and I found no lab page. 2025 paper: "Solving Satisfiability Modulo Counting Exactly with Probabilistic Circuits", ICML 2025 (homepage).
- **Yongle Zhang**: 6 PhD students on his Team page (yonglezh-purdue.github.io/team); Congyu Liu is co-advised with Pedro Fonseca. 2025 paper: "Understanding and Detecting Fail-Slow Hardware Failure Bugs in Cloud Systems", USENIX ATC 2025 (homepage).
- **Haoran You**: his Purdue profile lists no homepage. I found haoranyou.com by web search, and it links to his EcoAI Lab site. 3 PhD students who started in Fall 2026; I left out Joonhyung Lee, who starts in 2027. 2025 paper: "ORCHES: …", MICRO 2025 (lab publications page).
- **Z. Berkay Celik**: 6 PhD students: 3 he advises alone and 3 co-advised (2 with A. Bianchi, 1 with D. Xu). 2025 paper: "Spatiotemporal Consistency: A Universal Defense Against Attacks on Autonomous Systems", IEEE Security & Privacy Magazine 2025 (homepage).
- **Weiruo Zhang**: 3 PhD students on wrzlab.org/team-2; Rashmi Bhaskara is a Medical Physics student co-supervised with another professor. 2025 paper: a spatial cell–cell colocalization framework, Nature Communications 2025 (lab publications page).
- **Zachary Kingston**: 8 PhD students, but uncertain. The team page (commalab.org/members) redirects to the homepage, so I counted from how people describe themselves on the 34 individual member pages. Kevin Zhang and S. Talha Bukhari are co-advised. Shrutheesh R. Iyer's page still says "incoming", which may be out of date; I counted him. 2025 paper: "AORRTC: …", IEEE RA-L 2025 (lab publications page).

Scraped pages are saved under `/tmp/fceval-a4-t1-ycda4mmj/work/.firecrawl/hp/<slug>/`.

import json,glob,sys
t={o['slug']:o for o in json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))}
r={}
for f in sorted(glob.glob(sys.argv[2]+'/b*.json')):
    for o in json.load(open(f)): r[o['slug']]=o
print(len(r), set(t)-set(r))
rows=[]
for s,o in sorted(t.items(),key=lambda kv: kv[1]['name'].split()[-1].replace(',','')):
    x=r[s]
    hp=x.get('homepage_url'); lab=x.get('lab_url')
    page=f"[{hp}]({hp})" + (f"; lab: [{lab}]({lab})" if lab and lab!=hp else '')
    c=x['phd_count']; cs=x.get('phd_count_source_url')
    cnt=(f"{c} ([src]({cs}))" if cs and c!='not listed' else str(c))
    if x.get('phd_notes'): cnt+=' — '+x['phd_notes'].replace('|','/').replace('\n',' ')
    pap=f"\"{x['paper_2025_title']}\" ({x['paper_2025_venue']}) [{x['paper_source_type']}]({x['paper_2025_url']})"
    prof=f"https://www.cs.purdue.edu/people/faculty/{s}.html"
    rows.append(f"| [{o['name']}]({prof}) | {o['dir_title']} | {'; '.join(o['areas'])} | {page} | {cnt} | {pap} |")
    if x.get('notes'): rows.append(f"|  | | | | *Note:* {x['notes'].replace('|','/').replace(chr(10),' ')} | |")
open(sys.argv[3],'w').write("| Name (dept profile) | Title (dept directory) | Research areas (as listed) | Lab / personal page | Current PhD students | 2025 paper |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n"+'\n'.join(rows)+'\n')
EOF
python3 -I ../scripts/merge.py .firecrawl/table.json results purdue_ml_nlp_faculty.md; wc -c purdue_ml_nlp_faculty.md; python3 -I -c "
import json,glob
for f in sorted(glob.glob('results/b*.json')):
  for o in json.load(open(f)): print(o['slug'],'|',o['phd_count'],'|',o['phd_count_source_url'],'|',o['paper_2025_url'])"

**Things to know before you email:**
- **Who may not be advising at Purdue:** Clifton is emeritus. Bareinboim (Columbia), Honorio (Melbourne) and Shahbaz (now at Michigan) are adjuncts based elsewhere. Neville's homepage says she works mainly at Microsoft Research. Li's homepage says he has been on part-time leave at Perplexity AI since Feb 2026.
- **Who the list leaves out:** I included only people the directory tags with the AI/ML/NLP area. A few people whose names you might expect have other tags or none, such as Petros Drineas, Ilia Sucholutsky and Tunazzina Islam. I didn't check whether their own pages describe ML or NLP work.
- **How much to trust the counts:** I double-checked two counts myself (Ruqi Zhang 8, Ribeiro 3) against the saved pages and they matched. The other counts came from automated helpers reading each page and weren't rechecked by hand. Rows marked ⚠ come from outdated, mixed or unlabeled lists, so treat them as rough. "Not listed" means I found no student list on their pages.
